description:
## Why

A `pub fn` in production code reads as API. A future agent cannot tell that a helper
exists only so a test can look inside, so it gets reused and the test-only surface
becomes load-bearing. The production build should not contain it.

## Signal

dead_code already proves no pub(crate)/pub(super)/private function is test-only: in a
non-test lib build such an item has zero callers and warns, and cargo build is clean
under -D warnings. The blind spot is fully-pub items, which the lint exempts as public
API. 47 of those have no non-test caller.

## The integration-test constraint

tests/ (aot_variadic_open, fixture_matrix, fz2_cli) compiles against the lib as an
EXTERNAL crate and cannot see #[cfg(test)] items. The test files themselves cannot
move into the lib: all three use env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fz2"), which cargo defines only
for integration-test targets, and fixture_matrix is harness = false with libtest-mimic
generating trials dynamically. They are black-box tests that spawn the built binary,
so tests/ is also correct on the merits.

The fix is therefore to move the SUPPORT, not the tests.

## Work

1. Extract src/compiler2/fixture_metadata.rs (475 lines) to a workspace crate consumed
   as a [dev-dependencies]. It imports only std::fmt and std::path::Path -- completely
   standalone -- and has zero production consumers; mod.rs merely re-exports it. Both
   lib unit tests and tests/fixture_matrix.rs then share one copy, and it leaves the
   production lib. This removes the only reason any of these functions are pub rather
   than pub(crate). Cargo permits the dev-dependency cycle.

2. Gate src/compiler2/fixture_facts.rs (458 lines) as #[cfg(test)] in place. Do NOT
   extract it: it imports World, LoweredBody, ActivationKey, SemanticOrd and
   CallSiteSummary, so a separate crate would force those public and create a larger
   surface than the one being removed. Its only consumers are lib unit tests
   (fixture_contract_harness_test, fixture_facts_test); no integration test uses it.
   Consequence: transport_test.rs lists fixture_facts.rs among "production order
   owners" for a source-discipline scan; that entry goes with the gating.

3. Move causal.rs's formula_totals, product_totals and functions into tests/fz2_cli.rs
   as local helpers. They are plain aggregations over already-public event data, so
   they need no lib privileges. causal.rs itself stays production (public_trace.rs and
   pull.rs consume it).

4. Move the remaining 42 unit-test-only methods into #[cfg(test)] impl blocks on their
   own types. They are methods, not free functions, so they cannot literally move into
   a test file. cfg(test) beats narrowing to pub(crate): the item does not exist in a
   production build, so reuse is a compile error rather than a judgment call, and
   cfg(test) items stay visible to unit tests across modules.

## Not in this bucket: compile_root_jit

compile_root_jit has 0 production callers while its three sibling front doors ship
(run_root_interp 4, run_root_jit 2, compile_root_aot 1). That is not test scaffolding
-- it is either dead public API or a three-path parity gap. Decide it on its own
merits; do not silently cfg(test) a front door.

## Goal

933 lines of harness support leave the production lib and no test-only pub surface
remains, with no carved-out exceptions. After that dead_code alone is a sufficient
gate and this scan never needs repeating.

## Origin

Found while merging main into fz-tfn/long-lived-recalculator (PR #118). The merge
applied the rule where it bore on a conflict: emitted_executables was deleted once
main removed its only consumer, and a test-only RootId import moved out of production
scope into the test module that uses it.
title: Move test-only helpers out of the production surface
